33.0.0.en: "Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and thou that plunderest, and they did not plunder thee. When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end of plundering, they shall plunder thee." [1].

33.0.1.en: The woe here is directed against Assyria, and also against Babylon, as against every enemy who exalts himself against God and His people. Though his plan of destruction and plunder is carried out without hindrance, and without any harm touching him, yet this work falls under the woe.

33.0.2.en: God uses this destroyer as a rod of discipline for His people for a time, then returns to judge him. He leaves him to accomplish the desire for destruction that is in his heart, but as he has done, so it is done to him, so that ruin comes upon him and he is plundered at the appointed time.

33.0.3.en: Here it is fitting for us to realize that every hand stretched out to destroy has its work come down upon its own head, and drinks from the very cup that it fills for others. But their evil is turned to good for the children of God; even Satan himself cannot crush them, but his opposition to them becomes the cause of their victory and their crown. As St. John Chrysostom says: [The righteous are proved all the more when they are in the midst of those who want to turn them away from the life of righteousness and draw them toward evil, and yet they hold fast to virtue. The (Apostle) says, "For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you" (1 Cor 11:19). For this reason God left the wicked in the world, so that the splendor of the righteous may increase. Do you see the greatness of the gain? But this gain comes from the courage of the righteous, not of the wicked... Let us apply this argument to Satan also, for God left him here so that we may return to a stronger state, so that He may make the wrestler manifest and the struggle great. So when someone asks you, why did God leave Satan here? answer him with these words: that Satan not only does no harm to a man who is watchful and careful, but even benefits him, not by the intention of Satan (the wicked one), but because of the courage of him who makes good use of Satan's evil... Let your intention be good, and no one will ever harm you, but you will receive a great gain, not from the righteous only, but from the wicked also].

33.0.4.en: Christians have also realized that Satan collapsed completely after the Cross, so that ruin came upon him after he had been a destroyer of souls.

33.1.0.en: 2 O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble. 3 At the noise of the tumult the people fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations were scattered. 4 And your spoil shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar: as the running to and fro of locusts shall he run upon them. 5 The LORD is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness. 6 And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure. 7 Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without: the ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly. 8 The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man. 9 The earth mourneth and languisheth: Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down: Sharon is like a wilderness; and Bashan and Carmel are scattered.

33.1.1.en: When the prophet sees the ruin that comes upon the people of God, who deserve discipline, and the plundering of them by their enemies, he lifts up a prayer on behalf of the holy remnant, declaring in their name their waiting for the Lord, in which he says:

33.1.2.en: a. Asking for God's mercies and His salvation: "O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble" [2].

33.1.3.en: In the name of the devout people, the prophet lifted up a prayer for the military leaders who had fallen into distress and affliction because of Sennacherib and his army. "Be thou their arm every morning"; the literal translation is "be their arm every morning," a wonderful expression that reveals God's saving role in people's lives. He does not disregard their arms, even though they are as nothing and utterly unable to work; rather, He works by them as though they were His own arm. He takes them as His own, sanctifies them by His Holy Spirit, and supports them with heavenly power so as to save. He is the One who works in the lives of His believers, yet without disregarding them or destroying their energies, but through their sanctification.

33.1.4.en: * God wants the servant to appear as though he had contributed something, lest he fall into shame.

33.1.5.en: * Grace is always ready! It seeks those who receive it with all welcome. So when our Lord sees a soul that is watchful and burning with love, He pours out His riches upon it in abundance and plenty that surpass all its requests.

33.1.6.en: * God asks of us a small cause, so that He Himself may do the whole work.

33.1.7.en: St. John Chrysostom. This divine arm is a continual daily work in the life of the Church, as in the life of every member, "for his compassions fail not. They are new every morning" (Lam 3:22-23).

33.2.0.en: b. Asking for divine intervention, for it is enough for God to speak, and the Assyrians or others cannot bear the divine voice, so they flee. "At the noise of the tumult (roaring) the people fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations were scattered" [3]. By the mere utterance of a divine word the wicked tremble and flee; the mere appearance of God in the battle scattered the hostile nations.

33.2.1.en: How much we need the word of God to be proclaimed in the heart, so that evil flees and the powers of darkness are scattered, and the Crucified One to be revealed within us, so that sins and all evil spirits flee, and the Lord alone reigns in our depths.

33.3.0.en: Before the appearing of the Lord on the field and His uttering a word, the invaders became like the caterpillar (the larvae of the butterfly) and the locust, fleeing in shame and disgrace, while the people of God gather them [4]. Perhaps by the caterpillar he meant the dead and wounded of the Assyrian army, whom the people gather so that they may not cause a plague, and by the locust those who flee, so they run after them to catch them without any need of weapons. It is shame and disgrace for the enemy who destroyed and plundered with cruelty and arrogance!

33.4.0.en: c. The sanctifying of the city so that it becomes the righteous city of God, or the city of righteousness, in which God Himself dwells as "judgment and righteousness" [5]. It is filled with peace, security and salvation, with wisdom and knowledge. Its true treasure is "the fear of the LORD" [6]. This is a fear that springs from love, the fear of wounding the feelings of the Father, and not the fear of a slave toward his master, nor of a hired servant toward the owner of the house or of the work.

33.5.0.en: Now, after the prophet has asked God, in the name of the people, to intervene to crush the enemy and save the people, he sets out before God what has befallen the city, perhaps to move His divine compassion [7-9].

33.5.1.en: a. The heroes of war had no way to move, but stopped at crying out in helplessness and fear [7].

33.5.2.en: b. The ambassadors of peace wept bitterly [7] because Sennacherib broke the covenant. Hezekiah had paid a large sum so that he would leave the land, and yet he sent his army to storm it (2 Kgs 18:4, 17).

33.6.0.en: c. The highways lay waste [8] because everyone feared that the enemy would meet them on the road; for the reports of the messengers had come declaring the gravity of the situation, and the enemy had surrounded all the cities.

33.6.1.en: d. They entered into humiliation, so the cities became despised [8].

33.6.2.en: e. Barrenness occurred even in the most fertile and delightful regions, so that they became like the desert... Fruitlessness and barrenness are considered a disgrace, a sign of God's anger. Among these regions are Sharon, Bashan and Carmel.

33.6.3.en: When the prophet, in the name of the devout, took refuge in God, lifting up prayer for His divine intervention and confessing the ruin and devastation that had befallen the land, God intervened to condemn the enemy, Assyria. It is as though God longs to support us against the enemy, the devil, and is able to save us, but He waits for us to take refuge in Him and ask for His work with us, for He does not compel us even to our own salvation. He sanctifies the freedom of our will, longing that we ask by our own choice. As St. John Chrysostom says: [God does not force us, nor does the grace of the Spirit compel our will, but God calls us and waits for us to come to Him in our full freedom, and if we draw near He grants us all His help].

33.7.0.en: 10 "Now will I rise, saith the LORD; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself. 11 Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, as fire, shall devour you. 12 And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire." 13 Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might. 14 The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites: "Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?"

33.7.1.en: Though God is patient with the wicked, yet when the measure is full He judges them:

33.7.2.en: a. God Himself leads the battle: "Now will I rise, saith the LORD; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself" [10]. What man is unable to do, the Lord Himself does, out of His jealousy for the weak and the oppressed, counting their enemies as His enemies, as it is said, "Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away... But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God: yea, let them exceedingly rejoice" (Ps 68:1-3).

33.8.0.en: b. The judgment that comes upon them is the natural fruit of their deeds, for since they conceive chaff they bring forth not wheat but stubble [11], which is offered to the devouring fire. And since they breathe out violence like fire, they burn themselves [11].

33.8.1.en: Their works are chaff and thorns, good for nothing, and your threats are a blazing fire; therefore they carry within them the chaff and the thorns together with the fire, to become a blazing furnace not for others but for themselves!

33.8.2.en: If their evils, especially hypocrisy, are a devouring fire [1], then by this they practice, of their own will, the pledge of the everlasting burnings (fires) [1].

33.8.3.en: Just as righteousness carries its reward within it, and so brings the human soul into a pledge of eternal glory, so evil carries its reward within it, and so brings the soul into a pledge of the eternal fire of Gehenna.

33.8.4.en: Many of the Fathers of the Church see that virtue needs no reward because it carries its reward within it. As the martyr Justin says: [Does not virtue lead to the fulfillment of happiness? And St. Gregory of Nazianzus says: [For virtue to be virtue, it must have no reward]. Perhaps the secret of this is that the Fathers looked at virtue as an enjoyment of unity with Christ, as Origen says: [Virtue is for us to be one with Christ, for He is the virtues that fill Him], He is justice, wisdom and truth; so whoever practices virtue partakes in the divine nature, and this is the fullness of reward.

33.8.5.en: Vice is an imitation of the enemy of good and a sharing with him in his traits, together with a deprivation of the enjoyment of the Savior and of being like Him... and in this are the fruit of sin and its recompense.

33.9.0.en: 15 He that walketh in truth, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil; 16 He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure. 17 Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off. 18 Thine heart shall meditate terror: "Where is the scribe? where is the receiver? where is he that counted the towers?" 19 Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand. 20 Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken. 21 But there the glorious LORD will be unto us a place of broad rivers and streams; wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby. 22 For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us. 23 Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not well strengthen their mast, they could not spread the sail: then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey. 24 And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.

33.9.1.en: If God in His justice is a devouring fire that consumes the evil that carries corruption within it, and glorifies the believers who carry within them the righteousness of Christ, then He judges the wicked who persist in their evil and protects His righteous ones from their hands.

33.9.2.en: The prophet presents to us the traits of the righteous man, which are:

33.9.3.en: a. He walks in truth and righteousness, that is, he walks in Christ Jesus, the Way and the Truth, who is our righteousness.

33.9.4.en: b. He speaks uprightly [15]; his words declare his Gospel hidden in his heart.

33.9.5.en: c. He despises the gain of oppressions.

33.9.6.en: d. With disdain he shakes his hands from accepting a bribe.

33.9.7.en: e. He stops his ears from listening to plans that drive to the shedding of blood.

33.9.8.en: f. He shuts his eyes from looking upon evil.

33.10.0.en: g. He lifts up his heart to the heights to dwell with his Savior in the heavenly places [16].

33.10.1.en: h. He always takes refuge in his Christ as in the munitions of rocks that protect him from evil.

33.10.2.en: i. He is generous in giving, even out of his own needs: bread and water.

33.11.0.en: Such a man, who is sanctified by the Lord Christ to live pure with all his senses, whose depths are lifted to the heights, and who practices a life of fellowship with God and continual giving, deserves to enjoy the sight of the Lord Christ in His glories, for it is said, "Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty" [17]. This is the greatest gift to the righteous: to behold the Messiah in His splendor!

33.11.1.en: Some think that the talk here is about King Hezekiah, who enjoyed a special splendor when his heart rejoiced at seeing the destruction of Sennacherib's army, but the text is clear here that it speaks rather about the Lord Christ, who was glorified on the Cross, drawing the Gentiles to Himself and granting them a new nature: in place of enmity they bore love and friendship, in place of fierceness they became gentle, and in place of the strange language of evil they began to speak with a heavenly accent, for it is said: they became gentle, and in place of the strange language of evil they began to speak with a heavenly accent, for it is said:

33.12.0.en: "Where is the scribe? where is the receiver? where is he that counted the towers?" [18]. Where is the scribe who counts the army and records the names of the soldiers? And where is the receiver who determines the tribute that is paid to the enemy? Where is he who counted the towers in order to set guards over them and watchmen who observe the enemy and warn of the battle? All these energies have been turned from working for war and resistance into calm, peaceful energies working for the sake of the Kingdom of God, through their acceptance of faith in the Lord Christ.

33.13.0.en: "Thou shalt not see a fierce people" [19], for the works of the old, violent man have been removed so that we may bear the traits of our Creator through our enjoyment of the new man who is renewed every day.

33.13.1.en: "A people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive, dull of a tongue that is not understood" [19]; they received a new tongue, the language of the Spirit, the tongue of love and unity with understanding and wisdom.

33.13.2.en: And now, what is the work of the King, the Messiah, in the life of the Gentiles who come to Him by faith in Him?

33.14.0.en: a. "Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities" [20]. In place of the old terror of the scribe who records the army and the receiver, Zion becomes a city of joyful feasts, in which the people gather with constant gladness for common worship and for meeting with God Himself, our unceasing feast.

33.14.1.en: b. "A tabernacle that shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken" [20], that is, firm and established, which not even death can destroy, for it remains eternal.

33.15.0.en: c. Surrounded by rivers and streams on every side [21], which makes it fruitful in the Spirit.

33.15.1.en: d. It cannot be approached or fought against; for there sail in the waters surrounding it no small ships to spy on it and no great warships [21].

33.16.0.en: e. Christ the Lord Himself is the judge, the lawgiver, the king and the Savior [22]; He gave the constitution of the Gospel, reigned on the Cross and saved us, and still intercedes for us as our propitiation by His precious Blood.

33.17.0.en: f. Its enemy becomes like a broken ship in the midst of the waters, so that the enemy cannot raise its mast or spread its sail [23].

33.17.1.en: g. They defeat the enemy with power, so that even the lame are able to plunder him [23].

33.18.0.en: h. There is no sick person in it [24].

33.18.1.en: i. Its inhabitants receive the forgiveness of sins [24].

33.18.2.en: This is the picture of the soul that is joined to the Lord Christ: it becomes Zion, the joyful city of God, filled with gladness and peace, firm in the Lord, surrounded by the Spirit of God, the Holy One, who turns it into a fruitful paradise. Satan cannot defeat it, nor can the enemy of good destroy it. The Lord Christ declares His Kingdom in it, being its King, its judge, its lawgiver and its Savior. It overcomes the enemy of good and crushes him; no spiritual sickness can strike it; and finally it enjoys the forgiveness of sins through constant repentance.
